'''Boris Zilber''' ({{langx|ru|Борис Иосифович Зильбер}}, born 1949) is a Soviet-British mathematician who works in [[mathematical logic]], specifically [[model theory]]. He is an emeritus professor of mathematical logic at the [[University of Oxford]].

He obtained his doctorate ([[Candidate of Sciences]]) from the [[Novosibirsk State University]] in 1975 under the supervision of Mikhail Taitslin<ref>[http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=61237 Boris Zil'ber] at [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref> and his habilitation ([[Doctor of Sciences]]) from the [[Saint Petersburg State University]] in 1986.<ref>[https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/boris.zilber Prof. Zilber's page at the University of Oxford]</ref>

Zilber received the [[Senior Berwick Prize]] (2004) and the [[Pólya Prize (LMS)|Pólya Prize]] (2015) from the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners List of LMS prize winners]</ref> He also gave the [[Tarski Lectures]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Group in Logic and the Methodology of Science - Past Tarski Lectures|url=https://logic.berkeley.edu/past-tarski-lectures.html|access-date=2021-11-02|website=logic.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

==Research==

Zilber is well known for his seminal work around several fundamental problems in mathematics, mostly in the broad area of geometric [[model theory]].<ref>{{Citation | last=Kennedy| first=Juliette | title=
Boris Zilber and the model-theoretic sublime | journal = Model Theory | number = 2 | volume=3 | year=2024 | pages=305–315 | doi=10.2140/mt.2024.3.701| arxiv=2306.14562 }}.</ref> In particular, his trichotomy conjecture on the nature of strongly minimal sets has been extremely influential in geometric stability theory.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Pillay|first1=Anand|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=k6FK_Gqal2EC|title=Geometric Stability Theory|date=1996|publisher=Clarendon Press|isbn=978-0-19-853437-2|language=en}}</ref> Although it is false in full generality (refuted by [[Ehud Hrushovski]]), it holds in many important settings, e.g. [[Zariski geometry|Zariski geometries]], and has been successfully applied to several problems including the Mordell-Lang conjecture for function fields.<ref>{{cite book
 | editor-last = Bouscaren
 | editor-first = Elisabeth
 | date = 14 March 2009
 | title = Model Theory and Algebraic Geometry: An introduction to E. Hrushovski's proof of the geometric Mordell-Lang conjecture
 | url = https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68521-0
 | series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics
 | publisher = Springer Berlin, Heidelberg
 | pages = 216
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-540-68521-0
 | isbn = 978-3-540-68521-0
 | volume = 1696
	}}</ref> Zilber's work on model theory of complex exponentiation led him to propose several influential conjectures including the Quasiminimality conjecture,<ref>{{Citation | last=Wilkie| first=Alex| title=
Analytic continuation and Zilber's quasiminimality conjecture | journal = Model Theory | number = 2 | volume=3 | year=2024 | pages=701–719 | doi=10.2140/mt.2024.3.701| arxiv=2306.14562 }}.</ref> the [[Existential Closedness conjecture]],<ref name = "VAECZP">{{Citation | last=Aslanyan | first=Vahagn | title=
The Existential Closedness and Zilber–Pink conjectures | journal = Model Theory | number = 2 | volume=3 | year=2024 | pages=599–624 | doi=10.2140/mt.2024.3.599| arxiv=2403.09304 }}.</ref> and the [[Zilber-Pink conjecture|Conjecture on Intersections with Tori]].<ref name = "VAECZP"></ref>
